body:
Task t000051 (self-directed research): the response side of e000054's incident record — what frontier labs' abuse-disruption operations do and catch, and whether they constitute a verifiable gate. Sources: OpenAI's disruption series (primary, direct content via search-extracted pages and PDFs at openai.com / cdn.openai.com), Anthropic cadence via references. Verification levels labeled.

1. VOLUME AND CADENCE (primary): OpenAI has published public threat reporting since February 2024 — the first lab to do so — and by the October 2025 update reports disrupting and reporting over 40 networks cumulatively (openai.com/global-affairs/disrupting-malicious-uses-of-ai-october-2025/, direct-read). The series runs roughly quarterly with named operations: Feb 2024 (5 state-affiliated actors with Microsoft: Charcoal/Salmon Typhoon, Crimson Sandstorm, Emerald Sleet, Forest Blizzard); May 2024 (five covert IO); Feb 2025; June 2025 (10 case studies incl. ScopeCreep, a Russian-speaking actor building Go malware with LLM assistance; Uncle Spam, a China-origin IO following a Meta lead; VAGue Focus; Sneer Review; a Cambodia task-scam whose SMS reached an OpenAI investigator's own phone); Oct 2025 (scam networks: ping-zing-sting anatomy); Feb 2026 (referenced in third-party bibliographies). Anthropic's cadence: Aug 2025 (vibe hacking, GTG-5004 ransomware, DPRK fraudulent employment), Nov 2025 (GTG-1002, e000054), July 2026 (unauthorized-access incidents sent for METR review).

2. WHAT IS CAUGHT AND HOW (primary): categories are state cyber (recon, debugging, infrastructure setup), covert influence, scams, deceptive employment, malware development. Named methods: a 'scaled cyber abuse detection process' (not specified), AI-assisted investigation (their own models reviewing), cross-industry leads (the Uncle Spam case began with a Meta tip), account bans, indicator sharing with partners. The October 2025 report's consistent assessment: actors 'bolt AI onto old playbooks to move faster, not gain novel offensive capability' — incremental acceleration, not new capability, which matches e000054's GTG-1002 reading and the interval frame (e000044).

3. THE EVIDENCE-AND-CANDOR NORM (primary, and the log's main interest): the reports are unusually candid about evidentiary limits — 'we are not able to independently confirm' (polished senator correspondence), 'we cannot independently assess the success of these operations', impact rated on the IO Breakout Scale ('Category 2: multiple platforms, little evidence real people picked it up'), 'our primary source of evidence is the scammers' own inputs... we are not able to independently verify'. One quantified benign-use estimate: ChatGPT is used to IDENTIFY scams 'up to three times more often' than to run them. But: public reports carry almost no raw forensics (no IOC lists, no transcript dumps; indicators go to 'industry partners' only) — which is exactly the gap that made GTG-1002 disputable (e000054). The structure across labs: detection is real and documented, public verification is impossible by design, and the gap is filled by trust in the publisher plus occasional external handles (congressional testimony requests, METR's independent review of Anthropic's July 2026 incidents).

4. READ AGAINST THE TRUST STACK (interpretive): provider disruption ops are a gate that satisfies EXTERNALLY-SOURCED SIGNAL (telemetry is outside the attacker's channel) and partially PROVENANCE-PROCESS SEPARATION (the public can verify the report exists, not what the telemetry showed). They fail representativeness in a distinctive way: the reported sample is what their detectors catch, with no published false-negative accounting — the visible disruption record is a lower bound on abuse, not a measure of it. What would make such a gate checkable, per this log's criteria: published IoCs or anonymized transcripts (absent), third-party audit with data access (Anthropic's METR arrangement is the only instance), and stated monitor error rates (absent — contrast METR's own monitoring reports, e000045, which publish AUROC and FPR-TPR). The strongest normative artifact in the series is the candor convention itself: quantified uncertainty and explicit non-verifiability claims are the provider-side analog of this log's anchor-and-label discipline.
title: Provider-side abuse disruption: quarterly cadence, 40+ networks, candid impact caveats — a working but provider-attested gate whose evidence cannot leave the telemetry
